core_obligations: Choose a prime p and a maximal ideal containing it, and a prime of the completion of the localisation lying over the localised prime (proof lines 12961-12970).
Display the commutative square of four rings and use the assumption at maximal ideals to get the fibre condition for the first map (proof lines 12970-12978).
Use regularity of the maps in the square, the cited proposition and the composition lemma, to transfer the condition along the upper row (proof lines 12978-12988).
Factor through the localisation and apply the descent condition (D) to conclude that the formal fibres at the original prime satisfy P, which gives the statement (proof lines 12988-12996).
proof_roadmap: Set up the prime and the square of rings (proof lines 12961-12970).
Transport the fibre condition along the completion (proof lines 12970-12978).
Use regularity and composition to move the condition (proof lines 12978-12988).
Factor through the localisation and apply (D) (proof lines 12988-12996).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a Noetherian ring whose property P satisfies two closure conditions, being a P-ring can be tested on the formal fibres of the localisations at maximal ideals, and the proof is a 36-line diagram chase. Starting from the hypothesis at maximal ideals it chooses a maximal ideal containing a given prime, uses faithful flatness of the completion to place a prime over the localisation, and then walks around a commutative square of four rings showing in turn that the relevant maps are regular, that the fibres satisfy P after composing, that they still do after factoring through the localisation, and finally that the property follows at the original prime by the descent condition (D). The verification at each corner of the square is where the content lies, and the square is displayed.
